meta.subtitle: FFY 2025 Overview
meta.description: A statewide snapshot of advocacy, complaint resolution, outreach, resident engagement, and systems work completed during Federal Fiscal Year 2025.

informationEducation.intro: The annual report provides direct FFY 2024-to-FFY 2025 comparisons for four information, education, and training activities. Original counts remain visible below; no percentage change is inferred.

comparisons.label: Information and assistance to facility staff

residentVoice.title: The 29th Annual VOICES Forum
residentVoice.summary: The resident-led forum connected residents with policymakers, regulators, advocates, and state agency leaders. Residents advanced priorities through the Personal Needs Allowance campaign, work to strengthen resident councils, and direct legislative and systems advocacy.

metrics.label: Individuals receiving individualized information and assistance

communityOmbudsman.summary: Because staffing and appropriations limited the program's scope, work focused on education, individualized information and assistance, navigation, warm handoffs, and coordination rather than full case intervention in every matter.
communityOmbudsman.coordination: Regional and multi-agency work addressed Home and Community Based Services, residential care homes, waiver requirements, discharge planning, and coordination across facility-based and community-based systems.

closures.summary: Closures and evacuations heightened the need for informed choice, resident-centered transition planning, continuity of relationships, proximity to established supports, and coordination intended to reduce transfer trauma.

categories.label: Federal Funds
categories.note: Includes Older Americans Act Title VII and Title III funds.

categories.label: Other Federal Funds, ARP Title VII

funding.note: Older Americans Act Title VII and Title III amounts are components of Federal Funds and are not added again above. Bar lengths are calculated from the annual report's stated funding amounts.

highlights.title: Resident-directed advocacy
highlights.summary: Complaint work, policy priorities, and public participation remained grounded in resident direction and self-determination.

highlights.title: Transfer and discharge education
highlights.summary: Training addressed updated notice, portal submission, placement, appeal, and discharge-planning responsibilities.

highlights.title: Resident legislative participation
highlights.summary: Residents provided testimony and engaged lawmakers on personal needs, staffing, resident rights, and quality of life.

highlights.title: Strengthening resident councils
highlights.summary: The program supported resident-led councils as platforms for shared problem-solving, education, and advocacy.

highlights.title: Community Ombudsman expansion
highlights.summary: Education, navigation, warm handoffs, and cross-system coordination continued within limited staffing and appropriations.

highlights.title: Emergency and closure response
highlights.summary: Ombudsman representatives supported resident choice, continuity, proximity to known supports, and safer transitions.

highlights.title: Home and Community Based Services coordination
highlights.summary: Regional and multi-agency work connected discharge planning, waiver requirements, community supports, and resident protections.

highlights.title: Fear of retaliation
highlights.summary: Fear of retaliation remained an ongoing barrier to raising concerns and using complaint pathways across long-term care settings.

highlights.title: Legislative and systems advocacy
highlights.summary: The program advanced resident protections, stronger oversight, emergency safeguards, and cross-setting accountability.
